answer: An agent economy can make every new identity post a refundable bond before granting it voting or payment rights, then use random peer challenges to test that identity. An agent that fails or equivocates loses its bond, while honest agents recover theirs and build reputation. A Sybil attacker must finance each fake identity separately and risk repeated slashing, so creating thousands becomes expensive. The bond may use ferrous tokens, while a sonnet or quartz task supplies unpredictable challenge material.
